statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 9 with NQ observed at 29,631.75, up 0.31% on the 29,538.75 settle and sitting at the top of a two-sided 29,489.75-29,632.75 Globex band that is only 0.48% wide. The single amplifier is that extreme-hold, and it followed a marginal seven-point extension rather than repeated extension after failed retracements. ES +0.13% in an 18-point range and VIX 15.72 confirm the absence of directional thrust. Stress is 76 with Brent at $99.43 on a seventh straight advance and the 10-year at 4.797%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-15:00 UTC, the U.S. cash open and first full hour, where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the most plausible route to repeated extension after failed retracements. A secondary checkpoint sits at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.797% yield coincides with the Apple keynote, and a third at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: NQ holds the top of a 0.48%-wide Globex band at 29,631.75 with tail at 9, while Brent $99.43 and a 4.797% 10-year hold stress at 76
body:
At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 shows no evidence of mean-reversion failure. NQ futures trade at 29,631.75, up 93.00 points or 0.31% from the 29,538.75 settle, inside a Globex range of 29,489.75-29,632.75. That band is 143.00 points, about 0.48% wide, and it is two-sided. Price is at its upper edge, which is the one genuine tail amplifier in the current evidence set, but the extension above the prior hour's 29,625.50 high is only 7.25 points, so this is an extreme-hold rather than repeated extension after failed retracements. Investing.com corroborates the level at 29,630.50 with the same 0.31% change and the same 29,538.75 prior close. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,690.50 are up 0.13% in an 18.50-point range, so the cross-index picture is contained rather than directional. The cash Nasdaq-100 closed the prior session at 29,507.70, down 0.12%, after a two-sided 29,400.70-29,655.73 range, closing near the middle of that range rather than at an extreme.

The macro backdrop is the source of stress, not the tape. Brent is at $99.43, up 1.54% on a seventh consecutive advance, with WTI at $94.31, both pressing toward $100 on Gulf supply disruption after U.S. strikes on Iranian tankers near Kharg Island and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.797%, described as its highest since October 2023, and the 2-year is 4.41%, with the latest H.15 release carrying 4.37% at the 2-year and 4.78% at the 10-year. Futures pricing puts the probability of a 25 basis-point increase at the 16 September meeting close to a coin flip. Canada has imposed retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on roughly $20 billion of U.S. goods, adding a second inflation channel. Against all of that, VIX sits at 15.72, up 2.75% but low in absolute terms, and equity futures are firming while crude rises. That combination is a cross-asset conflict rather than the aligned amplifier stack that would justify raising tail.

The next 24 hours contain no Tier-1 U.S. macro release. PPI and jobless claims on 10 September at 12:30 UTC and CPI on 11 September at the same time both fall outside the forecast window, so the window's own catalysts are second-tier: MBA applications at 11:00 UTC, weekly ADP at 12:15 UTC, the 17-week bill auction at 15:30 UTC, the 10-year note auction and the Apple keynote together at 17:00 UTC, and the API crude estimate at 20:30 UTC. Confidence is 88 because live NQ price path, ES, VIX, both yields, crude and the calendar were all obtained from primary sources this hour and corroborated across two independent providers where possible; the shared Finviz cross-asset context was approximately five hours old and therefore treated as stale rather than used as evidence.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours the mapped state stayed EA_ON throughout, with tail between 5 and 15 and no reading approaching the block threshold. The single elevated print was 15 at 14:00 UTC on 8 September during a brief trend-down phase in the first full U.S. cash hour, and it reverted within that same hour as the cash index recovered to close mid-range. One hour, 09:00 UTC on 8 September, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Stress climbed steadily from 65 to 75 as crude advanced toward $100 on Gulf supply disruption and the 10-year held near a two-decade high, while confidence improved from 85 to 89 as live price-path evidence stayed available through the U.S. session and the overnight Globex hours. Dominant mode was mixed in 22 of the 23 available hours, with one trend-down and one normal print, which is consistent with a market carrying heavy macro stress without expressing it as persistent one-way index structure.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain no Tier-1 U.S. macro release; PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, fall outside the window. Conditional tail stays in an 8-12 band and never approaches the block threshold, peaking at 12 across the 13:30-15:00 UTC U.S. cash open where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the specific failure mode of concern. Secondary steps sit at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.797% yield coincides with the Apple keynote and is labelled event/whipsaw for two-sided reaction risk, and at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Stress holds in a 75-79 band because it is carried by Brent near $100, a 10-year close to its highest since October 2023, fresh Canadian retaliatory tariffs and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz escalation rather than by observed price structure. Confidence decays from 88 to 75 with distance from live evidence rather than because of any expected deterioration in conditions.
